owasp_category: A08:2021 - Software and Data Integrity Failures
description: routes/fileUpload.ts's handleYamlUpload accepts a .yml/.yaml complaint attachment from anyone, unauthenticated, and deserializes it with js-yaml's yaml.load() inside a 2-second vm sandbox. The per-call timeout caps a single request's cost, but nothing limits how many such requests one caller can fire concurrently. A classic billion-laughs YAML (nested anchor/alias expansion) sent five times in parallel from one script measurably stalls the whole server: an unrelated GET to the product search endpoint went from 0.17s at rest to 9.9s while the bombs were parsing, a real, shared-event-loop denial of service, not just an isolated slow request. Juice Shop's own catalog does track a narrower slice of this (yamlBombChallenge, category 'Insecure Deserialization', flips on a single successful 2-second timeout), but has no challenge for the concurrent-request amplification that turns a capped single-request cost into a real service outage.
expected_exploit_indicator: An unrelated legitimate request's response time increases by an order of magnitude or more while several YAML-bomb uploads are being parsed concurrently
expected_blocked_signal: After a small number of .yml/.yaml uploads from the same caller in a short window, further ones are refused before reaching the backend parser, and an unrelated request's response time stays close to its unloaded baseline
legitimate_check: A normal complaint upload (a plain .pdf, no YAML involved) and ordinary API traffic are not slowed or blocked by the control.
